```python
def max_sub_array_sum_repeated(a, n, k):
    arr = a[:n]
    best = 0
    cur = 0
    for i in range(n * k):
        cur += arr[i % n]
        if cur < 0:
            cur = 0
        best = max(best, cur)
    return best


assert max_sub_array_sum_repeated([10, 20, -30, -1], 4, 3) == 30
```

This follows the team note: it walks all n*k positions of the virtual array, reads `a[i % n]`, and resets the running sum to 0 when it goes negative. It returns 30 for the assert case. Because the running sum can reset to 0, an all-negative input returns 0 (the empty subarray), not the largest single element. My earlier version handled that case differently.
